title: The Concept of Quantum Entanglement
text:
Quantum entanglement describes a physical phenomenon where two or more particles become linked in such a way that they must be described with reference to each other, regardless of the spatial distance separating them. Measuring a property, such as spin or polarization, on one particle instantaneously dictates the corresponding property of the other entangled particle.

This correlation is non-local, meaning the influence appears simultaneous across space, challenging classical notions of locality and separability. Einstein famously termed this phenomenon 'spooky action at a distance' due to its apparent contradiction with relativistic speed limits for information transfer.

While entanglement itself cannot be used to transmit classical information faster than light, it forms the foundational resource for emerging quantum technologies, including quantum cryptography (QKD) and quantum computation.
